question: What is the primary cause of pressure ulcers in bedridden patients?

options.A: Prolonged pressure on soft tissue over bony areas
options.B: Excessive moisture from daily bed baths
options.C: Frequent movement of the patient by nurses
options.D: Lack of daily protein intake in hospital diets

explanation: Continuous pressure compresses blood vessels, stopping blood supply to the skin and underlying tissue until damage occurs. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do midwives use specialized bed accessories for vulnerable patients?

options.A: To redistribute body weight and protect sensitive skin
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for turning patients
options.C: To keep the hospital bed sheets permanently warm
options.D: To shorten the total duration of hospital admission

explanation: You've got this! Bed accessories help spread out body weight and reduce friction, keeping your patient comfortable and safe from skin breakdown. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of using a bed cradle?

options.A: To keep the weight of heavy bedclothes off the patient's skin
options.B: To prevent the patient from rolling out of bed at night
options.C: To elevate the patient's head for easier breathing
options.D: To secure intravenous lines away from the patient's hands

explanation: Think of a bed cradle as a protective tent over the body. It lifts blankets so they don't press against tender wounds or sensitive limbs. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient with severe second-degree burns on both legs is admitted to your ward. Which bed accessory should you request?
explanation: A bed cradle is a lifesaver here! It keeps the heavy bedsheets from touching and irritating the burned skin surfaces. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is a common challenge when a bed cradle is used on a patient's bed?

options.A: The patient's blood pressure will automatically drop within an hour
options.B: The metal frame will block all routine nursing observations
options.C: The bed sheets will become permanently stained with rust
options.D: The patient may feel cold because air circulates under the raised blankets

explanation: Lifting blankets away from the body lets trapped heat escape. You just need to add a light extra cover to keep your patient cozy! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which action is essential right after setting up a bed cradle for a patient?

options.A: Applying antiseptic cream to the entire lower body daily
options.B: Locking the patient's door to prevent visitors from moving the frame
options.C: Ensuring the frame is secure and does not pinch or scratch the patient
options.D: Removing all pillows from the bed to maintain proper body alignment

explanation: Patient safety first! Always double-check that the metal or wooden structure is stable and has no sharp edges that could cause injury. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h3)

question: What shape is a traditional air-ring cushion?

options.A: Rectangular with firm wooden side borders
options.C: Circular like a donut with a hollow center
options.D: Cylindrical like a long bolster pillow

explanation: Exactly right! Air-rings are round inflatable cushions with an open center designed to let a sore body part float over empty space. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why do modern wound care guidelines often advise against using traditional air-ring cushions?

options.A: They are too expensive for standard use in most government hospitals
options.B: They always pop within the first two hours of patient use
options.C: They make it impossible to perform bed baths properly
options.D: They can concentrate pressure on the outer ring and cut off blood flow to surrounding tissue

explanation: It seems counterintuitive, but the hard edges of a ring cushion can press hard against surrounding skin, cutting off circulation and making ulcers more likely. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h4)

question: What happens when an air-ring cushion is pumped up with too much air?

options.A: It becomes hard and increases pressure on the skin instead of relieving it
options.B: It loses its circular shape and turns into a flat mat
options.C: It automatically deflates itself to a safe level within minutes
options.D: It becomes softer and more comfortable for the patient

explanation: Over-inflating takes away the gentle 'give' of the cushion, turning it into a hard surface that actually hurts vulnerable bony points. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why should you always put a cloth cover over a rubber air-ring before using it?

options.A: To prevent direct skin contact, sweating, and friction
options.B: To increase the height of the cushion for taller patients
options.C: To make the cushion look more decorative in the ward
options.D: To prevent the air inside from escaping through the valve

explanation: Bare rubber sticks to the skin, traps heat and sweat, and quickly leads to skin irritation. A simple cover prevents this! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the main reason to document your use of bed accessories in a patient's chart?

options.A: To prove to hospital management that the ward has enough equipment
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of the patient's admission
options.C: To replace the need for verbal handovers between nursing shifts
options.D: To ensure clear continuity of care and record skin conditions

explanation: Good charting helps your team! Documenting what devices you used and how the skin looked guides the next shift of caregivers. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why must you stick to regular turning schedules even when your patient is using a pressure-relieving bed accessory?

options.A: Turning schedules are only required for patients who refuse to use bed accessories
options.B: Accessories lose all their pressure-relieving power after exactly one hour
options.C: Accessories assist with comfort but do not replace the need to relieve pressure by repositioning
options.D: Regular turning is only done to change the bed sheets, not for skin health

explanation: No accessory can do it all! Bed aids are wonderful helpers, but manual repositioning is still your best tool to completely prevent pressure ulcers. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T4#BMP110_U4_T4_h6)
